When Water and Forests Redraw the Map: A New Model for Regenerative Roads

August 19, 2026 Inter-American Development Bank regenerative roads, nature-based solutions, Latin America, Guatemala, deforestation, infrastructure resilience, IDB, landscape-scale NbS, CA-9 North
Read the source article

Quick summary

The Inter-American Development Bank is advancing a "regenerative roads" model in Latin America that combines resilient grey infrastructure with landscape-scale nature-based solutions, using Guatemala's CA-9 North corridor as a pilot to demonstrate that forest conservation at the watershed level can be 16× more cost-effective than repairing damage.

Key takeaways

  • Road infrastructure in Latin America faces a threefold challenge: poor logistics performance, growing natural hazard exposure, and accelerating natural capital loss
  • The IDB's regenerative roads model combines resilient grey infrastructure with nature-based solutions at the landscape scale
  • Maintaining forested buffer zones near roads can be 16× more cost-effective than repairing damage
  • Guatemala's CA-9 North corridor pilot connects Atlantic and Pacific ports, carrying 71.5% of the country's exports
  • 49% of Guatemala's roads face severe landslide risk exacerbated by deforestation within watersheds
